What It Means For You: Every candidate now moves through a clear, comprehensive, configurable set of stages (Screening through Offer) instead of ad-hoc tracking.

Feature: Approve / Reject / Hold with mandatory reason
What It Means For You: Every decision at every stage requires a reason, is logged for audit, automatically emails the candidate, and notifies the team.
Admins can add or reorder stages, outcomes, and rejection reasons from a screen -- no developer needed for routine changes.

Feature: Close a candidate's journey from any stage
What It Means For You: Recruiters can now formally close out a candidate (withdrawn, backed out, not selected, etc.) from wherever they are in the process, not only at the Offer stage.
A candidate closed by mistake can be reopened instead of starting the record over.
Recruiters can pause a candidate's journey and it is correctly excluded from reminders and automated sweeps while paused.
The header notification bell is now visible and working -- recruiters, HR and admins get notified of pipeline events (new reviews, feedback due, offers, etc.) as they happen.
Candidates who go quiet on a document request, and approvers sitting on a pending offer, now get automatic follow-up emails instead of relying on someone remembering.
On the Staging server, no email can ever reach a real candidate -- every send is automatically redirected to an internal test inbox, so UAT is safe to run end-to-end.
HR uploads one CSV export from Evalground and the system automatically matches every row to the right candidate, records the score, and (optionally) auto-approves or rejects on the pass mark.
Booking an interview (Outlook calendar invite + Teams link + reminders + scorecard) now works for every round: Technical 1, 2 and 3, HR, and CEO / Final
Each interviewer records structured feedback online; the HR round scorecard now matches the full paper evaluation form field-for-field.
All interviewers' feedback on one candidate is rolled up into a single summary with a recommendation tally, so the next round doesn't have to dig through separate forms.
Per company decision, the Client round is tracked in the system for record-keeping, but the system never emails the client or generates an invite -- everything is still coordinated offline.
Zeko HR-screening and functional-interview scores now sync automatically; the pipeline screen updates live the moment a score arrives, with no manual refresh needed.
HR requests documents (payslips, address proof, ID) with one click; the candidate uploads them via a secure link with no login required.

Feature: Verify or reject with a reason
What It Means For You: HR verifies each document or rejects it with a reason -- a rejected item automatically re-opens for the candidate to re-upload, with the reason shown to them.
Candidates who don't respond get reminded automatically. Documents are never deleted, in line with our retention policy.

Sharing the offer with the candidate, and the candidate's accept/reject decision are all tracked in one place with a full audit trail (appointment letters themselves are still handled by HR outside the system, as before).
Once every opening on a role is filled, the requisition automatically closes and drops off the open-roles list; if an acceptance is later reversed, it automatically reopens.
A journey automatically closes 90 days after a candidate's joining date if nobody has closed it manually.

Feature: Vendors now get real status updates
What It Means For You: Placement vendors finally receive automatic, content-free status updates on the candidates they submitted.
Vendors get a milestone note when an offer happens (no figures or details) and nothing at all during the Documents stage, protecting candidate privacy.
The rule protecting a vendor's ownership of a candidate they submitted for 90 days now holds, including when duplicate candidate records are merged.

Feature: Vendor Dashboard shows real pipeline stages
What It Means For You: Vendors see the actual current stage of their candidates instead of a guessed status.
Zeko pass-rate, time-to-hire, and two other Analytics figures were launched; all four report accurate, verified numbers.
The Search Candidates page was decluttered to Name / Email / Phone, sorted newest first, removing confusing options that didn't add value.
Recruiters see and can edit the exact shortlist/reject email -- with a proper formatting toolbar -- before it goes to the candidate, instead of it firing automatically.
Every rejection now requires a reason (with a free-text option when 'Other' is picked), strengthening the audit trail.

Feature: Tag to an Open JD on keyword search
What It Means For You: Shortlisting or rejecting from a keyword search now requires tagging the real open role, so the candidate's email and all reporting name the correct position instead of 'Manual Screening'.
Candidate search no longer silently caps results (previously capped between 50 and 3,000 depending on the search) -- recruiters now see every matching candidate.
Recruiters can choose whether a shortlist or reject action sends a candidate email at all.
A rejected candidate is held out of search results for 90 days -- rather than forever, or not at all -- before they can resurface for reconsideration.

Feature: Shortlisted / Rejected by X on Y
What It Means For You: Every candidate card and detail view now shows exactly who made the shortlist or reject decision, and when.
A new dashboard chart shows how many candidates each recruiter added versus shortlisted, giving managers visibility into individual throughput.
If the AI candidate-ranking service is temporarily busy, recruiters now see a clear 'showing top N of M matches, service busy' message instead of a confusing partial result.
A role cancelled by the business can now be closed with a reason, instead of sitting open in dropdowns indefinitely.

Feature: Board filters and real email conversations
What It Means For You: Recruiters can filter the board to 'Rejected only' or 'My candidates', and can view and reply to the actual Outlook email conversation with a candidate directly from their record.
